codes.sample: Cross-sectional community survey, April 2023. Adults aged 18 or older in purposively chosen southern Thai communities with high kratom use (N=169; 93.5% Muslim). 45 (26.6%) were current users, 23 (13.6%) former users and 101 (59.8%) never users. Current users: 86.7% male, mean age 41.8 years.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Self-reported current kratom use: "Current 45 (26.6)" (Table 1). Former users also completed the use-pattern section, but use patterns are reported only for the 45 current users.
codes.dependence_measures: No dependence or use-disorder instrument. Outcome is "harmful use" ("more than 20 leaves per day", a quantity cut-off). Single self-report items on burdens in the past month (increased use, craving) and quit attempts. No DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS or ASSIST.
codes.possible_duplicate: Single sample from a community-medicine course project of the Prince of Songkla University medical school (southern Thailand, April 2023, n=169, 45 current users). No overlap with another publication is stated.
codes.note: "Harmful use" (>20 leaves/day; 22/45, 48.9%) is a cut-off on quantity used, not a dependence diagnosis. "Craving to use 9 (20.0)" (Table 2, p9) is a single item with no case definition. The questionnaire is in Supplementary S1 (not in this text), but the main text names no dependence scale.

codes.sample: 293 male ketum (kratom) leaf users in Penang, Kedah and Perlis, northern Peninsular Malaysia. Cross-sectional survey with non-probability sampling (purposive, quota and chain referral). Described as regular users, split into medium-term and long-term groups. Most were Malay. The inclusion and exclusion criteria (Ch. 3.7–3.8) are missing from the text received.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Regular ketum users, mostly drinking ketum juice ('designed to determine severity of ketum dependence in regular ketum users'). The exact definition of regular use and the medium/long-term cut-points are missing (Ch. 3.7, 4.3.3).
codes.dependence_measures: Leeds Dependence Questionnaire (LDQ), adapted for ketum and translated. The cut-off for 'severe' dependence (Ch. 3.11.1) is missing. Withdrawal (MWC), craving (MCQ-SF) and ASI-5 were also used.

estimates.threshold_or_category: Severe ketum dependence (cut-off not stated in text received)
estimates.quote: Fifty-five percent of the sample reported severe ketum dependence

codes.possible_duplicate: PhD thesis (D. Singh, USM, 2013): n=293 regular male ketum users in Penang, Kedah and Perlis. The likely article on the same sample is Singh, Müller & Vicknasingam 2014, Drug Alcohol Depend (kratom dependence, withdrawal, craving); citation from memory, not the text.
codes.note: The text stops in Ch. 2. Missing: Methods (LDQ scoring and cut-off, Sec. 3.11.1), Sec. 4.5.1, Table 4.4 (p. 145) and Fig. 4.7. Only the abstract figure (55% severe, n=293) can be extracted. We cannot tell whether 'severe' is a fixed cut-off or a split based on the sample's distribution (E3). The full thesis is needed for this and for the subgroup counts.

codes.sample: 395 active US adult kratom consumers who use kratom regularly, enrolled July–November 2022 in a nationwide remote NIH EMA study (baseline survey). 54.9% male, mean age 38.1, 81.3% White, mean 5.7 years of kratom use; 95.9% regularly used whole-leaf products.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current regular use: "US adults who use kratom regularly" / "active US adult kratom consumers". The text gives no exact frequency threshold for eligibility.
codes.dependence_measures: Kratom use disorder (KUD) assessed with the 11 DSM-5 SUD criteria applied to kratom (self-report survey). Lifetime and past-year KUD = 2+ symptoms; mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe 6+. SOWS (withdrawal only) was also used, but it is not a case definition for this review.

estimates.instrument: DSM-5 SUD criteria for kratom (11 criteria)
estimates.quote: Lifetime KUD criteria (2+ lifetime symptoms) were met by 63.5%

codes.possible_duplicate: Same NIH nationwide EMA sample of US regular kratom consumers (enrolled Jul–Nov 2022, n=395 at baseline). Related papers: Smith et al. 2024 (EMA, observed dosing), 2023a (methods), 2023b (interviews). Check whether they report KUD for this sample.
codes.note: Only percentages are printed; n=395 is assumed as the denominator. Counts are in Supplemental Table 1, which was not received. The abstract's "mostly in the mild/moderate range (80.7%)" does not match the subcategories clearly, so it was not extracted. No KUD prevalence is reported by sex.
